historical_record.description: One of a handful of buildings left standing in the Central SoMa area after the earthquake and fire, most of them steel-framed.
Remodelled during the Depression-era 'Modernize Main Street' campaign.
Recorded in the city's 2008 survey of the Transit Center District, adopted in 2012, as a contributor to the proposed New Montgomery, Mission & Second Historic District.
Refaced to designs by the architect John V.D. Linden, the failing terra-cotta ornament stripped away and replaced with fluted terra cotta and pared-back Art Deco detail.
Erected as a ten-story office building with ornate Renaissance and Baroque detail.
Architect Warren C. Perry established his own practice here, in the building that also housed John Galen Howard’s firm.
Repaired and put back into service after the 1906 earthquake and fire.

building.completed_conflict: The 2008 survey of this district dates the building to 1904; the assessor dates the building on this parcel to 1906.

unknowns: The inventory table in the same report dates this building to 1906.

The statement locates this 1931 remodel at "the northwest corner of 1st and Mission streets," while its earlier reconstruction is cited at 602-06 Mission Street; this entry treats them as the same Atlas Building.
